description:
In session.rs, during two-step SASL PLAIN authentication, when the client sends '*' to cancel the exchange (RFC 4954 §4), the code passes '*' to verify_sasl_plain which fails base64 decoding and returns None. This increments auth_failures and sends 535 Authentication credentials invalid instead of 501 as required by RFC 4954 §4.

RFC 4954 §4 states: 'If the client wishes to cancel the authentication exchange, it issues a line with a single "*". If the server receives such a response, it MUST reject the AUTH command by sending a 501 reply.'

Trigger: send EHLO, AUTH PLAIN (two-step), then respond with '*' to the 334 challenge. The server increments auth_failures. Three such cancels cause a forced disconnect.

Fix: check the response string before passing to base64 decoding; if it equals '*' (after trimming CRLF), send '501 5.7.0 Authentication exchange cancelled' and continue the loop without incrementing auth_failures.
title: smtp: AUTH PLAIN cancel (*) treated as failed credentials
